requirements_summary: Workloads: low-latency chat agent (p50 < 150ms target), embeddings batch generation (500 req/min), document reranking.
Data residency: all production inference and logs must remain in EU region; no cross-region key material replication without explicit signoff.
Key control: BYOK mandatory for production; customer CMK; support for AWS KMS (CMEK/envelope), Azure Key Vault (customer HSM/Dedicated HSM), GCP KMS with CMEK, and on-prem HSM via PKCS#11.
Audit: comprehensive key-access logs exported to S3/Splunk with 7-year retention; must include requestor identity and session context.
Authentication: SSO via Okta (SAML) required; SCIM for user provisioning preferred.
Network: VPC peering + private endpoints, strict egress rules; must be able to operate with no public internet access for key ops.
Operational: key rotation policy, emergency key revocation, and documented runbooks for incident response required.
Throughput/latency: ensure KMS integration does not add >10ms p50 overhead to token generation path; consider local envelope keys cached in HSM-protected memory.
Regulatory: financial regulator will audit key control — Redwood must provide architecture + evidence for key custody model used in POC and production.
Desired SLA: 99.95% uptime for inference endpoints; KMS availability constraints must be called out.
Encryption in transit: TLS mutual auth for any connections to customer's KMS endpoints; optional hardware-backed TLS via mTLS certs.
poc_plan: Week 1: Network setup and VPC peering; establish private endpoints to customer's KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP).
Week 2: Key provisioning and BYOK flow validation (create CMK, test grants, test envelope key creation).
Week 3: Integrate Redwood runtime to use CMEK for model artifact encryption and KV cache encryption; run functional tests.
Week 4: Load test inference with KMS calls instrumented, measure key access latency and overall p90/p50 token latencies.
Week 5: Security review with customer's auditors; provide audit log export and SIEM integration demo.
Week 6: Wrap-up, handoff docs, and review commercial terms for Dedicated/Private uplift and HSM add-on.
POC success criteria: keys remain under customer control, audit logs complete and exportable, latency targets met, and legal approves key ownership language.
